text: If bridge priorities are left at their defaults, which switch becomes the root bridge?
choices: The one with the most ports
The one with the lowest MAC address, which correlates with manufacturing date — usually the oldest switch
The one closest to the core
explanation: The oldest switch in the building, likely the least capable and quite possibly in a cupboard, now carries all inter-switch traffic. Setting the root bridge explicitly is one of the highest-value five-minute configuration tasks in enterprise networking, and it is skipped constantly.
